Guideline: Use the library theme system instead of global stylesheet overrides
Description: qfluentwidgets ships its own QSS per widget; a global setStyleSheet on the window or a base class overwrites the library styling and breaks light/dark switching
Do: Apply the library theme once at startup and let each component keep its own styling
Don't: Do not apply a global stylesheet that overwrites the library QSS
Code Good: Call setTheme(Theme.AUTO) once at startup and let components inherit their own styles

Guideline: Use ThemeColor presets for accent colors
Description: ThemeColor exposes a fixed preset set so light and dark variants stay consistent; hardcoded hex values drift from the theme
Do: Set a ThemeColor preset and let the library derive light and dark variants
Don't: Do not hardcode accent hex values that drift away from the theme
Code Good: Apply a ThemeColor preset through setThemeColor and read the accent back from the theme

Guideline: Size content cards to their content
Description: Adding stretch to a content card forces it to absorb leftover vertical space and produces large dead areas inside the card
Do: Let content cards take their natural height and absorb leftover space with one trailing stretch
Don't: Do not give content cards a stretch factor
Code Good: Give the card a content-driven height and let a single trailing addStretch absorb the remainder

Guideline: Use explicit spacing instead of implicit defaults
Description: Default Qt spacing is 6-10px which reads as cramped in a desktop utility; set spacing explicitly per container
Do: Set spacing explicitly on every container to match the design token scale
Don't: Do not leave the implicit Qt default spacing in place
Code Good: Set spacing on every container layout to match the design token scale

Guideline: Set a size policy so cards keep their intended height
Description: Without an explicit size policy a widget can grow beyond its content when placed in a stretchy layout
Do: Set an explicit size policy so a content card keeps its intended height
Don't: Do not let cards expand vertically by default
Code Good: Set QSizePolicy on content cards so they stay at content height

Guideline: Use QSizePolicy Maximum for content-sized vertical widgets
Description: A Maximum vertical policy lets a widget take only the space it needs while still expanding horizontally
Do: Use an expanding horizontal and maximum vertical policy for content-sized widgets
Don't: Do not make every widget expand in both directions
Code Good: widget.setSizePolicy(QSizePolicy.Expanding, QSizePolicy.Maximum)

Guideline: Use QPropertyAnimation for state transitions
Description: Qt animations run on the UI thread event loop and drive real widget properties; hand-rolled timer interpolation drifts and repaints needlessly
Do: Animate a concrete widget property with QPropertyAnimation
Don't: Do not hand-roll interpolation with a timer and manual repaints
Code Good: Animate a concrete property such as maximumWidth opacity or pos with a QPropertyAnimation
Code Bad:
anim = QPropertyAnimation(self, b'maximumWidth')
anim.setDuration(200)
anim.setEasingCurve(QEasingCurve.OutCubic)
anim.setStartValue(0); anim.setEndValue(320); anim.start()

Guideline: Use OutCubic for entering transitions and OutQuart for numeric counters
Description: Entering motion decelerates into place which reads as settling; a counter that eases out lands softly on the final value
Do: Use OutCubic for entering panels and OutQuart for numeric counters
Don't: Do not use an accelerating curve for an entering transition
Code Good: Use QEasingCurve.OutCubic for panels and QEasingCurve.OutQuart for counters

Guideline: Keep the animation object on the widget
Description: An animation created as a local variable can be garbage collected mid-flight and silently never run
Do: Keep the animation as an instance attribute on the widget
Don't: Do not create the animation as a throwaway local
Code Good: Store the animation as an instance attribute so it lives as long as the widget

Guideline: Guard against re-entrant animation triggers
Description: A click during a running animation restarts it and produces a visible jump
Do: Ignore a trigger while an animation is still running
Don't: Do not restart a running animation from its original start value
Code Good: Use a running flag or check isFinished before starting a new animation

Guideline: Never sleep on the UI thread
Description: time.sleep in a slot freezes the event loop and makes the whole window unresponsive
Do: Drive waiting with a QTimer or a worker thread
Don't: Do not sleep on the UI thread
Code Good: Drive waiting with a QTimer or a worker thread and never block the GUI thread

Guideline: Never use processEvents to fake asynchronous work
Description: processEvents re-enters the event loop and lets handlers run mid-operation which corrupts state
Do: Use a real QThread worker or a queued signal connection
Don't: Do not fake asynchrony with processEvents
Code Good: Use a real QThread worker or a queued signal connection

Guideline: Never touch widgets from a worker thread
Description: Qt widgets are not thread-safe; mutating them from a worker causes crashes and undefined rendering
Do: Emit a Signal from the worker and connect it to a slot on the widget
Don't: Do not mutate widgets from inside a worker thread
Code Good: Emit a Signal from the worker and connect it to a UI slot

Guideline: Throttle progress updates from a long scan
Description: A scan emitting a signal per file floods the event loop and stalls the UI
Do: Batch progress updates and emit at most every 100 ms
Don't: Do not emit one signal per scanned file
Code Good: Batch progress updates and emit at most every 100 ms

Guideline: Use a queued connection when the worker lives in another thread
Description: AutoConnection resolves to DirectConnection when both objects share a thread affinity which defeats the marshalling
Do: Connect across threads with an explicit queued connection
Don't: Do not rely on AutoConnection resolving correctly across threads
Code Good: Connect with Qt.QueuedConnection explicitly across threads

Guideline: Set a readable minimum body size
Description: Desktop utility text below 14px becomes dense and hard to scan at native DPI
Do: Keep body text at 14 px or larger and secondary text at 12 px
Don't: Do not drop body text below 14 px
Code Good: Keep body labels at 14px or larger and secondary labels at 12px

Guideline: Use the library label components instead of raw QLabel
Description: qfluentwidgets labels carry the theme font and colour roles; a bare QLabel does not follow theme changes
Do: Use the library label components so type and colour follow the theme
Don't: Do not use a bare QLabel for styled text
Code Good: Use BodyLabel StrongBodyLabel SubtitleLabel TitleLabel LargeTitleLabel CaptionLabel

Guideline: Set font size once per role not per widget
Description: Scattering setFontSize calls across widgets makes the type scale drift
Do: Define the type scale in one place and apply it per role
Don't: Do not scatter individual font size calls across widgets
Code Good: Define the scale in one place and apply it per role

Guideline: Use the library layout helpers for consistent spacing
Description: qfluentwidgets ships VBoxLayout HBoxLayout and GridLayout that apply its spacing and margins defaults
Do: Use the library layout classes so spacing is consistent across pages
Don't: Do not mix raw Qt layouts with library layouts on the same page
Code Good: Use the library layout classes so spacing is consistent across pages

Guideline: Use the library card components instead of custom QFrame
Description: SimpleCardWidget CardWidget and ElevatedCardWidget already carry the theme border radius and shadow
Do: Build grouped content on a library card that already carries radius and shadow
Don't: Do not hand-roll a card frame with a custom stylesheet
Code Good: Use a library card as the base for grouped content

Guideline: Use model view for large result lists
Description: Creating one widget per row for hundreds of entries is slow and memory heavy
Do: Use a model with a view for large result sets
Don't: Do not create one widget per row for hundreds of entries
Code Good: Use QAbstractListModel with QListView or QTableView for large sets

Guideline: Use a custom delegate for row rendering
Description: Delegates paint rows without creating widgets which keeps scrolling smooth at high row counts
Do: Paint rows inside a delegate so scrolling stays smooth
Don't: Do not render a widget inside the delegate paint method
Code Good: Implement QStyledItemDelegate and paint the row in paint and sizeHint
Code Bad:
class RowDelegate(QStyledItemDelegate):
    def paint(self, painter, option, index): ...

Guideline: Give every interactive row a visible hover and selected state
Description: Rows without distinct hover and selected states read as a static table and give no feedback
Do: Implement a distinct hover state and a stronger selected state
Don't: Do not leave rows without any hover or selected feedback
Code Good: Implement both states in the delegate and keep the selected state clearly stronger than hover
Code Bad:
def paint(self, painter, option, index):
    if option.state & QStyle.State_Selected: ...

Guideline: Give destructive actions a confirm step and a distinct affordance
Description: Actions that permanently delete need to be visually and behaviourally separated from safe ones
Do: Use the primary button for the main action and require an explicit confirm for destructive ones
Don't: Do not style a permanent delete as an ordinary action
Code Good: Use PrimaryPushButton for the main action and require an explicit confirm for destructive actions

Guideline: Never let the confirm dialog default to the destructive choice
Description: A dialog whose default button is the destructive one turns one stray Enter into a deletion
Do: Make the safe option the default so a stray Enter never deletes
Don't: Do not make the destructive button the default choice
Code Good: Make the safe option the default and require an explicit click on the destructive one

Guideline: Show progress during long operations
Description: An operation with no visible progress reads as a frozen application and invites duplicate clicks
Do: Show a determinate progress bar with a percentage and a remaining estimate
Don't: Do not leave a long operation with no visible progress
Code Good: Show a determinate progress bar with a percentage and a remaining estimate

Guideline: Keep the minimum hit area at 32 by 32
Description: Small icon-only buttons are hard to hit and look unfinished
Do: Enforce a minimum hit area on icon buttons and tool buttons
Don't: Do not shrink interactive controls below a usable size
Code Good: Enforce a minimum size on icon buttons and tool buttons

Guideline: Set an accessible name on icon-only controls
Description: An icon-only button exposes no text to screen readers and to voice control
Do: Set an accessible name on every icon-only control
Don't: Do not rely on a tooltip as the only accessible label
Code Good: Set accessibleName alongside the tooltip for every icon-only control

Guideline: Keep focus visible and reachable by keyboard
Description: Removing the focus ring makes keyboard navigation impossible to follow
Do: Keep the focus indicator and keep every control reachable in tab order
Don't: Do not remove the focus policy from interactive widgets
Code Good: Keep the default focus indicator and ensure every interactive widget is reachable in tab order

Guideline: Use QLabel buddy for form fields
Description: A standalone label is not associated with its input so screen readers announce it without the field
Do: Bind each label to its field as a buddy
Don't: Do not leave a standalone label next to an unbound input
Code Good: label.setBuddy(field)

Guideline: Use FluentWindow for the shell and addSubInterface for pages
Description: FluentWindow provides the title bar and the animated page switch
Do: Use FluentWindow for the shell and addSubInterface for the pages
Don't: Do not build the shell from a bare QMainWindow with a manual stack
Code Good: Register each page with addSubInterface and use the library icons

Guideline: Use the library icon set for navigation
Description: Mixing icon families breaks visual consistency; FluentIcon covers the common cases
Do: Map every navigation and action icon to a FluentIcon
Don't: Do not mix icon families or draw ad hoc glyphs
Code Good: Map each navigation entry to a FluentIcon

Guideline: Respect the system reduce-motion setting
Description: Users who disabled OS animations still need the interface to be usable even if transitions shorten
Do: Shorten or skip transitions when the system reports reduced motion while keeping the end state correct
Don't: Do not ignore the system reduce motion setting
Code Good: Shorten or skip transitions when the OS reports reduced motion while keeping the end state correct

Guideline: Do not add motion to every state change
Description: Animation on every widget turns an interface into noise; reserve it for changes the user initiated
Do: Animate only the changes the user initiated
Don't: Do not animate every state change on every widget
Code Good: Animate expand collapse selection and progress only

Guideline: Keep transition durations in the 160 to 220 ms band
Description: Shorter than 120 ms is perceived as a jump and longer than 300 ms feels sluggish for a local desktop app
Do: Keep panel and card transitions in the 160 to 220 ms band and press feedback at 100 to 150 ms
Don't: Do not use transitions long enough to feel sluggish
Code Good: Use 160-220 ms for panel and card transitions and 100-150 ms for press feedback

Guideline: Do not fill the viewport with equally weighted panels
Description: When every panel is the same size the interface reads as a dashboard with no hierarchy
Do: Give the primary task the largest area and let secondary panels shrink
Don't: Do not give every panel an equal stretch
Code Good: Give the primary task the largest area and let secondary panels shrink

Guideline: Prefer a card list over a multi-column table for categorical results
Description: A table with index column and checkbox column reads as a spreadsheet rather than a consumer utility
Do: Render each category as a card with an icon a title and a summary line
Don't: Do not use a multi column table with an index and a checkbox for categorical results
Code Good: Render each category as a card with an icon a title and a summary line

Guideline: Keep one visual focus per screen
Description: A screen with several equally large numbers has no reading order
Do: Make the single most important number large and the rest secondary
Don't: Do not give several numbers the same visual weight
Code Good: Make the single most important number large and the rest secondary

Guideline: Use QThread subclass with run for background work
Description: A QThread subclass moves the work into run while the GUI thread stays responsive
Do: Subclass QThread and emit a Signal when the work finishes
Don't: Do not run the work directly on the GUI thread
Code Good: Subclass QThread and emit a Signal when the work finishes

Guideline: Use QObject worker with moveToThread for long jobs
Description: A QObject worker moved to a thread supports queued signals and a clean shutdown
Do: Move a QObject worker to a dedicated QThread for a deterministic stop path
Don't: Do not leave a long job on the GUI thread
Code Good: A QObject worker moved to a dedicated QThread gives a deterministic stop path

Guideline: Signal and Slot are the thread-safe boundary
Description: Emitting a Signal from a worker thread marshals the call onto the receiver thread
Do: Declare a Signal on the worker and connect it to a slot on the widget
Don't: Do not touch the widget directly from the worker
Code Good: Declare a Signal on the worker and connect it to a slot on the widget

Guideline: Wait for a worker to finish before closing the window
Description: Exiting while a QThread is running raises QThread destroyed while it is still running
Do: Quit and wait for the thread before the window closes
Don't: Do not exit while a worker thread is still running
Code Good: Connect the worker finished signal to quit and wait before the window closes

Guideline: Guard the shutdown of a running worker
Description: Closing the app during an active scan leaves a half-written state
Do: Set the stop event and wait for the worker before the window disappears
Don't: Do not terminate the thread abruptly
Code Good: Track a running flag and stop the worker before the window disappears

Guideline: Use QMessageBox with an explicit safe default
Description: A default button on the destructive option turns a stray Enter into a deletion
Do: Make the cancel button the default and require an explicit click on the destructive one
Don't: Do not make the destructive button the default choice
Code Good: Make the cancel button the default and require an explicit click on the destructive one
Code Bad:
box = QMessageBox(QMessageBox.Question, 'Move to Recycle Bin', 'Move 120 items?')
box.setDefaultButton(cancel_btn)

Guideline: Show the concrete impact in the confirmation text
Description: A generic Are you sure gives the user no basis for a decision
Do: State the item count and the total size in the confirmation text
Don't: Do not ask a generic confirmation with no numbers
Code Good: State the item count and the total size before asking
Code Bad: QMessageBox.question(self, 'Move to Recycle Bin', f'Move {count} items ({size}) to the Recycle Bin?')

Guideline: Keep a modal dialog on top of its parent
Description: A dialog that opens behind the main window looks broken and can be missed
Do: Pass the parent widget so the dialog is centred and stays modal
Don't: Do not open the dialog without a parent
Code Good: Pass the parent widget so the dialog is centred and stays modal

Guideline: Use QAbstractListModel with QAbstractItemModel for result rows
Description: Building one widget per row for hundreds of entries is slow and heavy on memory
Do: Use a QAbstractListModel with QListView or QTableView for large result sets
Don't: Do not create one widget per row for hundreds of entries
Code Good: Use QAbstractListModel with QListView or QTableView for large sets

Guideline: Implement data as a model role rather than a custom widget subclass
Description: Model roles keep rendering in the delegate and avoid subclassing widgets for each row
Do: Expose the display text through a model role and override data
Don't: Do not subclass a widget per row type
Code Good: Expose the display text through Qt.ItemDataRole.DisplayRole and override data
Code Bad:
def data(self, index, role):
    if role == Qt.ItemDataRole.DisplayRole: return self.rows[index.row()].name

Guideline: Update models with beginResetModel and endResetModel
Description: Mutating a model outside a reset leaves the view showing stale rows
Do: Wrap a full reload in beginResetModel and endResetModel
Don't: Do not replace the row list without a reset
Code Good: Wrap a full reload in beginResetModel and endResetModel

Guideline: Use SearchLineEdit for search fields
Description: The library search field adds the clear button and the correct focus styling
Do: Use SearchLineEdit for any filter field
Don't: Do not use a bare LineEdit for a search field
Code Good: Use SearchLineEdit rather than a bare LineEdit for any filter field

Guideline: Give every input a label bound as buddy
Description: A label that is not associated with its field is announced without the field
Do: Bind each label to its field as a buddy
Don't: Do not leave a standalone label next to an unbound input
Code Good: Call setBuddy so the label and the field are linked

Guideline: Validate input before accepting it with a QValidator
Description: Silent coercion of a bad value produces a wrong result that is hard to trace
Do: Attach a QIntValidator or QDoubleValidator and show the reason inline
Don't: Do not silently coerce a bad value
Code Good: Attach a QIntValidator or QDoubleValidator and show the reason inline next to the field

Guideline: Show a determinate progress bar with a percentage and a remaining estimate
Description: An indeterminate spinner gives no sense of how long the operation will take
Do: Set a range and a value and pair the bar with a text summary
Don't: Do not use an indeterminate range for a known total
Code Good: Set a range and a value and pair it with a text summary

Guideline: Make the cancel action reachable during a long operation
Description: A user trapped by an uncancellable operation will force kill the app
Do: Offer a cancel button that sets the worker stop event and report that it was requested
Don't: Do not disable the cancel action during a long operation
Code Good: Offer a cancel button that sets the worker stop event and report that it was requested

Guideline: Distinguish a stale result from a fresh one
Description: Showing an old number as current misleads the user about what the app is doing
Do: Mark a snapshot as stale and say so next to the value
Don't: Do not present an old value as a current one
Code Good: Mark the snapshot as stale and say so next to the value

Guideline: Keep focus order matching the visual order
Description: Tab order that jumps around forces the user to hunt for the next control
Do: Set the tab order explicitly to follow the visual sequence
Don't: Do not leave the tab order to follow insertion order
Code Good: Set the tab order explicitly to follow the visual sequence

Guideline: Do not steal focus on a background update
Description: A background refresh that grabs focus interrupts typing
Do: Update the label text without activating the window
Don't: Do not steal focus during a background update
Code Good: Update the label text without calling setFocus or activating the window

Guideline: Move focus into a dialog when it opens
Description: A dialog that opens with focus on its close button invites an accidental dismissal
Do: Set the initial focus to the safe action inside the dialog
Don't: Do not open the dialog with focus on the destructive action
Code Good: Set the initial focus to the safe action inside the dialog

Guideline: Use QPainter with the antialiasing hint for custom painting
Description: Without antialiasing custom drawn shapes look jagged at native DPI
Do: Enable the antialiasing render hint before drawing custom shapes
Don't: Do not draw custom shapes without antialiasing
Code Good: Enable QPainter.RenderHint.Antialiasing before drawing

Guideline: Use devicePixelRatio for crisp output on high DPI screens
Description: Drawing at logical pixels makes custom art blurry on a scaled display
Do: Multiply by devicePixelRatio and set it on the pixmap
Don't: Do not draw custom art at logical pixels only
Code Good: Multiply by devicePixelRatio and set the device pixel ratio on the widget

Guideline: Prefer drawing a cached sprite over rebuilding gradients each frame
Description: Recreating a gradient every frame is the usual cause of a stuttering animation
Do: Build the sprite once and draw it each frame
Don't: Do not rebuild a gradient every frame
Code Good: Build the sprite once and draw it each frame

Guideline: Keep custom painting off the hot path when the view is hidden
Description: Painting a hidden widget wastes CPU and can keep a fan spinning
Do: Skip painting while the widget is not visible
Don't: Do not keep painting a hidden widget
Code Good: Skip painting when the widget is not visible

Guideline: Use FluentIcon for every navigation and action icon
Description: Mixing icon families breaks the visual consistency of the shell
Do: Map every action to a FluentIcon from the library
Don't: Do not mix icon families or draw ad hoc glyphs
Code Good: Map each action to a FluentIcon from the library

Guideline: Do not use an icon whose shape implies a different action
Description: An icon that reads as a pencil suggests editing even when the button deletes
Do: Pick an icon that matches the action and keep the tooltip consistent
Don't: Do not use an icon whose shape implies a different action
Code Good: Pick an icon that matches the action and keep the tooltip consistent

Guideline: Use QScrollArea for content that can exceed the viewport
Description: Without a scroll area the content is clipped and the lower part becomes unreachable
Do: Wrap the page content in a QScrollArea so nothing is cut off
Don't: Do not let content overflow the viewport silently
Code Good: Wrap the page content in a QScrollArea so nothing is cut off

Guideline: Keep the scroll area background transparent
Description: An opaque scroll area background creates a visible band that breaks the page
Do: Set the viewport background to transparent and match the page colour
Don't: Do not leave an opaque band behind the scroll area
Code Good: Set the viewport background to transparent and match the page colour

Guideline: Use a QStackedWidget for in-page mode switches
Description: Swapping page widgets on navigation makes the layout jump
Do: Keep one widget and switch its content inside a QStackedWidget
Don't: Do not remove and re-add page widgets to change mode
Code Good: Keep one widget and switch its content inside a QStackedWidget

Guideline: Keep the window minimum size large enough for the layout
Description: Setting a minimum below the content size causes clipping and overlapping labels
Do: Set a minimum size that fits the narrowest supported layout
Don't: Do not set a minimum size below the content size
Code Good: Set a minimum size that fits the narrowest supported layout
